title: Hill-climb any deliverable with the /council skill
description: council puts an agent's work in front of fresh reviewers that pick their own metrics, score it out of 10 and send it back until it passes.

title: Latency or throughput: the one dial behind LLM serving
description: How batching trades per-user speed for aggregate tokens, from one forward pass to a fleet, and how to choose which side to optimize.

title: Make decisions with the /decide skill
description: decide is an agent skill for hard choices like job offers: one pick, the fact that would flip it and a tripwire, plus what the model skips without it.

title: Job prep is mostly small things, done in the right order
description: An 80/20 plan for job prep with a CS degree. Pick the role, fix LinkedIn and the resume, rehearse the opening and close, then train each technical round.

title: My job search in numbers, and where the interviews came from
description: Thirteen weeks of my own records: 39 applications, 70 recruiter reach-outs, pass rates by interview round, and which route produced seven offers.

title: The verification layers behind Anthropic's 30,000 merges a day
description: Anthropic merges AI-written code at a rate no reviewer could read. How it checks that code, layer by layer, and which layers a team can copy.

title: Improving team efficiency at a high level
description: Giving everyone an AI tool makes individuals faster, not teams. Eight levels where a team's AI effort pays off, and why checking work sets the pace.

title: Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness and Hermes are built three different ways
description: One closed loop, a plugin kernel and a gateway daemon. Six ways to build an agent harness, what each lets you change, and why the score follows the plugins the model sees.

title: The AI stack, one constraint per layer
description: A roadmap of AI from power to product, covering what each layer runs short of, what to learn there, and how image, voice and world models differ.

title: Who builds the AI stack, and who is buying it
description: 158 AI companies placed on the stack and sorted by size, and why 2026's buyers were companies already on the same request path.

title: Predicting the future of AI stocks with economics
description: People adopted AI faster than the internet, but only about 2% of households pay for it. Where the money flows, and how I would position for the bull case.

title: Opus orchestrated, GPT agents built, and nobody graded their own work
description: How Claude Opus ran GPT-5.6 coding agents through a nine-hour build, and why the quality came from reviewers, not from the workers' self-scores.

title: Four predictions for how software teams will change
description: Smaller teams but more of them, internal tools that compete with SaaS, more self-hosted models, and engineers who own product decisions.

title: Why My Automated Trading Strategies Haven’t Earned Real Money
description: What my trading engine's tests actually showed, why positive returns weren't enough, and the agentic paper experiment I'm building next.

title: Why I optimize LinkedIn once a year
description: What changed after I updated my LinkedIn profile, which fields I focus on, and why I leave it alone between annual reviews.

title: How I build 3D that still behaves like a web page
description: How junxiong.dev uses Three.js with native scroll, one active canvas, reduced motion and a readable fallback.

title: How agent integrations get built inside large organisations
description: Registries, auth brokering, generated tool schemas and the org failure modes that stall internal agent platforms — grounded in public specs.

title: Where your tokens actually go in a coding agent
description: How files and tool output fill a coding agent's context, what long-context studies show, and how I would keep a session focused.

title: How I think about hardware for local models
description: Bandwidth, capacity, KV cache and MoE active parameters — the four numbers that decide local inference hardware, with sources.

title: Prefill and decode want different machines
description: LLM inference has two phases with opposite bottlenecks. Which one you care about decides what hardware to buy.

title: Why the same prompt can cost more on the next request
description: How prefix caching actually bills, what silently breaks it, and a worked cost example across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and the raw API.

title: What changes when you quantize a model
description: How quantization changes model size, speed and answers, and why weight memory and KV-cache memory need separate budgets.
